children: Morgan Stanley said its September consumer survey indicates that Walmart+ membership reached a new high. Notably, roughly 25% of respondents reported that they are Walmart+ members, which implies about 33.2M U.S. households, up approximately 1.6M from August's estimate of 31.6M. Because survey respondents may overstate membership, Morgan Stanley adjusted the estimate to about 21.6M households, or roughly 16% U.S. household penetration.

The firm noted that the three-month rolling measure suggests Walmart+ membership rose about 17% year over year in September, versus 16% in August. Growth has stayed in the mid-teens during 2026, slower than the low-30% range seen in 2025 but still consistent with Walmart's
recent commentary that membership fee revenue is growing at a double-digit rate.

"We believe these trends reinforce Walmart’s strong competitive positioning and its ability to attract incremental customers as consumers remain focused on value," highlighted analyst Simeon Gutman. "The membership ecosystem is supporting the growth of higher-margin revenue streams and positioning WMT to participate in emerging AI-enabled shopping opportunities through agentic commerce," he added.

trickled 0.2% lower in premarket trading to $104.06 vs. the 52-week range of $98.88 to $135.16. Wall Street analysts have a consensus Buy rating on WMT, but Seeking Alpha analysts are more cautious with a consensus Hold rating.
